trades.title: Coal Trimmer
trades.description: A dock labourer who worked in the hold of cargo ships, manually shovelling and leveling loose coal to ensure the vessel was evenly balanced and safe to navigate.

trades.title: Roller
trades.description: A skilled worker in iron and steel works who operated heavy rolling mills, guiding red-hot metal slabs through rollers to produce metal sheets, rails, or plates.

trades.title: Watchman
trades.description: A night guard employed by factories, docks, rail yards, or commercial premises to protect buildings, cargo, and raw materials from fire, theft, or trespass.

trades.title: Furnace Man
trades.description: An industrial worker responsible for fueling, monitoring, and maintaining the extreme temperatures of furnaces in foundries, gas works, and metal processing plants.

trades.title: Hoistman
trades.description: An equipment operator who managed industrial hoists and winches to lift materials, coal, or heavy machinery in dockyards, mines, and manufacturing plants.

trades.title: Wheelwright
trades.description: A craftsman who built and repaired wooden wheels for horse-drawn carts, wagons, and carriages, applying iron tires to secure the rim.

trades.title: Hawker
trades.description: A street trader who travelled through residential areas carrying goods, fruit, fish, or household items to sell directly to local residents.

trades.title: Weighman
trades.description: An official or industrial worker tasked with measuring and recording the weight of heavy goods, such as coal, timber, or grain, at docks and rail yards.

trades.title: Tube Worker
trades.description: An employee in metal manufacturing engaged in the production, finishing, or quality testing of iron, steel, or brass piping and tubes.

trades.title: Rivetter
trades.description: A metalworking artisan in shipyards and heavy engineering who secured steel plates together using red-hot metal rivets driven in by hand or pneumatic hammers.

trades.title: Stevedore
trades.description: A specialist dock foreman or quay worker responsible for managing the loading and unloading of ships' cargoes safely and efficiently.

trades.title: Linesman
trades.description: A technician responsible for laying, maintaining, and repairing telegraph, telephone, or electrical power cables along railways, streets, and industrial sites.

trades.title: Compositor
trades.description: A skilled print trade worker who arranged individual metal type letters into page layouts for newspapers, handbills, and commercial directory printing.

trades.title: Carman
trades.description: A horse-drawn vehicle driver employed to transport heavy goods, coal, and parcels between rail depots, docks, and local businesses.

trades.title: Wire Drawer
trades.description: A metalworker who pulled ductile metal rods through progressively smaller shaped dies to manufacture industrial wire, cables, and netting.

trades.title: Ganger
trades.description: A working foreman who led and supervised a gang of manual labourers on civil engineering projects, railway maintenance, or dock operations.

trades.title: Plate Layer
trades.description: A railway maintenance worker tasked with laying, inspecting, and repairing tracks, sleepers, and ballast across rail lines and sidings.

trades.title: Sugar Boiler
trades.description: A specialist confectioner or refinery worker who monitored and controlled the precise boiling and crystallization process of sugar syrup.

trades.title: Ostler
trades.description: A stable hand employed at coaching inns, commercial livery stables, or transport yards to feed, groom, and care for horses.

trades.title: Puddler
trades.description: A foundry worker who converted pig iron into malleable wrought iron by stirring molten metal in a reverberatory furnace with iron bars.

trades.title: Wardrobe Dealer
trades.description: A second-hand clothes merchant who bought, repaired, and resold cast-off clothing and household fabrics to working-class families.

trades.title: Berthing Master
trades.description: A maritime authority official who allocated specific mooring berths, managed ship traffic, and directed vessels arriving into docks and quays.

trades.title: Coal Tipper
trades.description: A dockyard operator who managed coal hoists and hydraulic tipping machinery to empty coal wagons directly into ship holds.

trades.title: Doubler
trades.description: A tinplate or steel mill worker responsible for folding over heated metal sheets during the rolling process to create thinner gauges.

trades.title: Waterman
trades.description: A boatman licensed to navigate small craft, ferries, or barges, transporting passengers and light goods across rivers, docks, and harbours.

trades.title: Wireman
trades.description: An electrical worker who installed, wired, and maintained internal electrical systems, motors, and lighting in industrial buildings and homes.

trades.title: Annealer
trades.description: A heat-treatment specialist in metalworks who heated glass or metal sheets and cooled them slowly to reduce internal stress and brittleness.

trades.title: Brick Burner
trades.description: A kiln operator responsible for packing, firing, and monitoring temperatures to bake raw clay into durable building bricks.

trades.title: Scavenger
trades.description: A municipal street cleaner or refuse collector employed to sweep roadways, clear refuse, and maintain town sanitation standards.

trades.title: Gas Stoker
trades.description: A heavy industrial worker who shoveled coal into retorts at municipal gasworks to produce coal gas for lighting and heating.

trades.title: Time Keeper
trades.description: An administrative clerk at worksites, docks, or factories who logged employee attendance, shift hours, and overtime for payroll.

trades.title: Sanitary Engineer
trades.description: A public health professional or contractor who designed, installed, and maintained urban drainage, sewer networks, and plumbing infrastructure.

trades.title: Slinger
trades.description: A dock or foundry worker who secured heavy loads to crane hooks using chains, ropes, and slings, guiding safer overhead movement.

trades.title: Vanman
trades.description: A transport driver who operated small horse-drawn or early motorized delivery vans to carry merchandise and goods to retail shops and homes.

trades.title: Herbalist
trades.description: A traditional medical merchant who prepared, blended, and sold natural botanical remedies, tisanes, and tonics to the public.

trades.title: Patternmaker
trades.description: A highly skilled woodworker or metalworker who crafted accurate 3D models used by foundries to create sand moulds for metal castings.

trades.title: Lamp Lighter
trades.description: A municipal worker who walked town streets at dusk and dawn to ignite, extinguish, and clean gas or oil street lamps.

trades.title: Verger
trades.description: A church official who assisted the clergy during services, managed church property, and cared for the parish grounds and buildings.

trades.title: Donkeyman
trades.description: A senior engine-room rating on steamships or docks responsible for operating auxiliary steam boilers (donkey engines) and winches.

trades.title: Boiler Scaler
trades.description: A manual labourer who climbed inside cool marine or industrial steam boilers to chip away hard mineral deposits and soot.

trades.title: Nail Cutter
trades.description: A machine operator or metalworker who cut wrought iron or steel strips into uniform lengths to produce cut nails.

trades.title: Sampler
trades.description: A commercial inspector who extracted representative samples of bulk commodities—such as grain, coal, or ores—for quality testing.

trades.title: Lathrender
trades.description: A woodworker who split straight-grained timber into thin, narrow strips (laths) to form the structural backing for lime plaster on interior walls and ceilings.

trades.title: Bar Dragger
trades.description: A heavy manual labourer in ironworks or rolling mills responsible for hauling and maneuvering heavy red-hot metal bars across the mill floor.

trades.title: Linotype Operator
trades.description: A skilled printing technician who operated a complex keyboard machine to cast complete lines of metal type ('slugs') from molten lead for newspapers and books.

trades.title: Hurdle Maker
trades.description: A traditional rural craftsman who split and wove coppiced timber, such as oak or hazel, into portable wooden fence panels used for livestock and agricultural boundaries.

trades.title: Cordwainer
trades.description: A shoemaker who crafted fine footwear from new leather, distinguished from a cobbler who primarily repaired existing shoes.

trades.title: Fettler
trades.description: A foundry worker who trimmed, filed, and cleaned rough edges, sand, and unwanted excess metal from fresh castings.

trades.title: Batcher
trades.description: An industrial worker responsible for measuring and mixing raw bulk ingredients in precise proportions before processing, commonly in glassworks, chemical plants, or concrete production.

trades.title: Berther
trades.description: A dockyard worker who assisted in guiding vessels into their designated berths and securing mooring lines at the quay.

trades.title: Capstanman
trades.description: An operator who managed mechanical or hydraulic capstans to haul heavy ropes, maneuvering ships along docksides or moving railway wagons around sidings.

trades.title: Sextoness
trades.description: A female church officer responsible for maintaining church property, managing graveyard interments, ringing the church bells, and preparing the building for services.

trades.title: Cupola Man
trades.description: A foundry worker in charge of loading and operating a cupola furnace, melting pig iron and scrap to produce molten metal for castings.

trades.title: Helve Maker
trades.description: A specialised woodworker who shaped durable wooden handles (helves) for axes, hammers, pickaxes, and heavy industrial hand tools.

trades.title: Botanist
trades.description: A professional or trade merchant dealing in medicinal plants, dried herbs, and botanical specimens, often running local apothecaries or herbal dispensaries.

trades.title: Journeyman Joiner
trades.description: A qualified, tradesman-level carpenter who had completed an apprenticeship, building intricate interior woodwork, doors, window frames, and furniture.

trades.title: Brakesman
trades.description: A railway worker responsible for manually operating the mechanical handbrakes on freight trains, shunters, or colliery trams to control speed.

trades.title: Pickler
trades.description: A tinplate or metalworks employee who immersed steel sheets into vats of acid to strip away scale and rust prior to tinning or galvanising.

trades.title: Roll Turner
trades.description: A highly skilled machinist who turned and shaped the heavy iron and steel rollers used in rolling mills, cutting exact grooves to form rails, bars, or structural girders.

trades.title: Pointsman
trades.description: A railway worker stationed along lines or in yards to manually shift track points, directing trains and shunters onto the correct set of rails.
